recipes.name: Pesto Chicken Florentine
ingredients_raw: 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut into strips
1 (4.5 ounce) package dry Alfredo sauce mix

steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium high heat. Add garlic, saute for 1 minute; then add chicken and cook for 7 to 8 minutes on each side. When chicken is close to being cooked through (no longer pink inside), add spinach and saute all together for 3 to 4 minutes.
Meanwhile, prepare Alfredo sauce according to package directions. When finished, stir in 2 tablespoons pesto; set aside.
In a large pot of salted boiling water, cook pasta for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente. Rinse under cold water and drain.
Add chicken/spinach mixture to pasta, then stir in pesto/Alfredo sauce. Mix well, top with cheese and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Pesto Chicken Florentine
raw_recipe.description: Spinach, chicken and pasta are smothered in a glorious creamy pesto sauce.

review.reviewBody:
Excellent!!! I've made this countless times. I use Classico brand basil pesto (small jar, green) and a jar of Classico brand Garlic Alfredo sauce. Instead of just the 2 cups of spinach, I use the entire bag of baby spinach leaves and add a couple of button mushrooms, sliced thinly. I sear my boneless, skinless chicken breasts first (sprinkled with creole seasoning/cayenne pepper for spiciness), and once they are cooked through I set them aside, wrapped in tin foil, until everything else is done, then chop them into bite sized pieces and toss them in the sauce. The chicken stays very moist and tender this way. I also like to throw some diced tomato (lightly salted) on top before serving. So delicious.

This is one of the best pasta dishes I've found on this site - definitely a keeper. Thanks for sharing!!!

Great recipe! I wouldn't cook the garlic with the chicken as it would burn at that temp and time. Instead I cooked the chicken in one pan and the garlic, spinach, and sauce in the other. I also added more spinach at the suggestion of others. I gave it four stars because I think it was a tad bland. Next time I will up the garlic and pesto.

Delicious! Following the suggestions of a few reviewers I seasoned the chicken with herb chicken seasoning before browning in Tuscan herb olive oil. After sautéing the garlic and browning the chicken I then removed the chicken from the pan and kept it hot in aluminum foil. I then added a little more EVOO, more minced garlic and 4 thinly sliced mushrooms. When the mushrooms were sautéed I added a bag of baby spinach and while that was sautéing I chopped up the chicken and added it back in. Also, I used the Buitoni 16 oz Alfredo sauce instead of making from a dry packet and Parmesan instead of Romano. My husband and I both loved it. And since it made such a large batch we will both have work lunches from it this week.

This was so good!! I used a whole bag of spinach, a jar of Alfredo, and a whole small jar of pesto. Then I added garlic powder, basil, onion salt, and pepper to the sauce. I heated the sauce in a separate pan. Then I added the chicken mixture to the sauce. Then when everything was done I took a small portion of the pasta water, then drained the pasta, and added everything to the pasta after it was rinsed. It tastes better when you marry the sauce with the pasta by using the starchy pasta water. I added 2 bags of cheese (4 cups). 2 cups of Parmesan and 2 cups of Mozzarella. My family loved it!!
Delicious & easy. Made my own Alfredo & Pesto. Added mushrooms and asparagus and more spinach. Used Fusilli pasta

This is a great go-to recipe. People often say it tastes like it came from a restaurant! I’ve made it so many times that I’ve simplified it quite a bit. I make regular Alfredo sauce with half and half, butter and Parmesan. If I’m feeling fancy, I roast cherry tomatoes and pesto in the oven; otherwise I open a can of petit diced tomatoes and spoon a big spoonful of pesto into the Alfredo sauce. I also add a package of frozen (thawed) spinach rather than fresh just because it’s easier to keep on hand and use in a pinch. I use a rotisserie chicken for the meat and mini penne for the pasta. It’s delicious! Looks fancy but requires little effort or prep!

Added onion, removed chicken from pan and deglazed with a little broth, then added back the chicken and continued. Made Hollandaise from scratch instead of Alfredo and added the pesto. Topped with pine nuts as well as cheese. Healthy? No. Delish? Absolutely!

Wonderful recipe to start from. I used chicken thighs, cut into thirds, as I prefer them to breast meat. After reading other reviews I tripled the spinach, doubled the pasta and added sliced crimini mushrooms. I also added a splash of toasted sesame oil to the pasta water which gave a lovely note to the penne. I seasoned the chicken with onion powder, salt & pepper and at the point of adding the spinach and mushrooms to the garlic & chicken, squeezed a half of a lemon into the mix. I didn't use the alfredo mix but a jar of Classico Alfredo to which I added my own fresh pesto. It was delicious right after making and absolutely divine the next day. So many variations to create. Have fun with this recipe!

This recipe turned out amazing. The only thing I will say is DO NOT rinse off the pasta. This is a travesty if you are Italian!! Rinsing off the pasta takes away all the starch. The sauce will coat better if you do not rinse. I added a 1/2 cup of chicken broth to the alfredo because it was too sticky.

I followed the recipe to a T but the chicken was bland so The next time I Mhar it made again I followed the recommendations, had it seared with salt,pepper and chili seasoning. The chicken was moist. As for the spinach, a 5oz tub is perfect with some mushrooms. My kids loved it and they paired with bulgogi.

It was VERY GOOD, I validated alil. I bought chicken strips cut that into cubes and seasoned the chicken with adobo, Cheyenne pepper, black pepper, garlic powder and paprika. I popped it in the freezer for 10 min to marinate faster. While the chicken was cooking I sauted the spinach in a small Dutch oven with salt and garlic. I used the whole bag of fresh spinach. Because it wilts down to nothing. This was actually very good. And will b making it again.

I made this substituting gluten free pasta and using jar alfredo sauce as many other reviewers have done. I could not locate the dry mix. This is a quick and easy dinner to put together. My daughter is a lover of jarred alfredo sauce and this was similar to something I usually make her. Using pesto to give the sauce a lil something extra was perfect and added to the quick and easiness of the recipe.
Great recipe. I breaded and baked the chicken because that's how my son wanted the chicken made. I added mushrooms and made homemade Alfredo sauce. Came out great

I couldn't ask for a more simple yet filling family meal! every time I visit my family they always ask for me to make this meal! I did experiment and tried it with mushrooms and ah the flavor would burst on your taste buds! This is a wonderful recipe for beginner cooks too.

Overall good weeknight family dinner. I would drain most of the juices from the cooked chicken so as not to loosen the alfredo. I used a jarred alfredo sauce instead of the dry mix. I also made a larger batch using a whole box of pasta and 2 chicken breasts sliced thin.

I made this recipe for the first time and loved it! I plan to make it part of our regular winter meal plan. For the chicken, I coated it in the creole seasoning recipe here (https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/38214/creole-seasoning-blend) by shaking the chicken with seasonings in a plastic zipper bag before cooking. I also added mushrooms but might also consider adding sauteed asparagus and diced tomato next time. The best part is that BOTH KIDS enjoyed it!

Made this last week for dinner and have had to make it 3 more times since then. My BF works out of town and asked me to make it for him and freeze it so he can enjoy it for dinner. He texted me a pic of him eating it and said "flipping delicious!!" That made me so happy!!! Thank you for a wonderful pasta dish that the whole family loved!!!!
Everyone loved it, even Riley.

I adjusted the recipe so I could do it in the slow cooker. So was a lot of sauce, I boiled noodles for only half the time and then let them finish cooking in the slow cooker. The absorb the sauce and was delicious.
Was very good. I use a jar of alfredo sauce instead of the packet, will double sauce next time as we like sauce!!! Will make again!
